intervals.quote: The AGS became the world's premiere accelerator when it reached its design energy of 33 billion electron volts (GeV) in July of 1960.

intervals.note: A bound, not an end-of-run date: the run was over by the date of the PRL paper. BNL dates the discovery to 1962.

quantity.quote: Although the maximum energy of the accelerator was 30 GeV, it was necessary to run it at 15 GeV in order to minimize the background from energetic muons.

name: AGS two-neutrino experiment
notes: The late-1959 conception of the experiment is in Schwartz's Nobel lecture ("The first conception of the experiment was in late 1959"); no source consulted gives the dates of the run.
No collaboration record: a seven-author Columbia group (Danby, Gaillard, Goulianos, Lederman, Mistry, Schwartz, Steinberger), with BNL on the author list. No detector record (not assigned).
BNL dates the discovery to 1962 on its Nobel page; the 1999 BNL Bulletin timeline (not used) gives 1963 for related items. The paper is dated 1 July 1962.

physics_goals.quote: perhaps the neutrinos from pion decay could be produced in sufficient numbers to allow us to use them
physics_goals.value: Produce a beam of high-energy neutrinos from pion decay and study how they interact

physics_goals.quote: Observation of High-Energy Neutrino Reactions and the Existence of Two Kinds of Neutrinos
physics_goals.value: Establish whether there are two kinds of neutrino

summary.plain: Physicists from Columbia University used Brookhaven's brand-new AGS accelerator to make the first beam of high-energy neutrinos, sent it through a thick steel wall into a spark chamber, and found that the neutrinos made muons, not electrons. Reported in 1962, it showed there are two kinds of neutrino.
summary.technical: Neutrino beam from pion decay: an internal AGS proton beam on a beryllium target, run at 15 GeV, a ten-ton aluminium-plate spark chamber behind a 13.5 m steel shield. 29 of 34 single-track events were muons from neutrinos, while only 6 shower candidates appeared where 2/3 × 29 would be expected if there were one neutrino type (Schwartz Nobel lecture).

unique_capabilities.quote: The experiment's use of the first-ever neutrino beam paved the way for scientists to use these particles in research at the AGS and around the world.
